ko.name: 국악한마당
ko.summary: 국악한마당은 국악을 통해 우리 민족 전통예술을 체험할 수 있는 공연이다. 매년 10월 개최되는 국악한마당에서는, 국악 명인공연, 세시풍속 및 전통문화 체험 프로그램, 국악 학습관 등을 통해 보고, 즐기고, 체험할 수 있는 다양한 장이 마련된다.
ko.description: ※ 해당 행사는 2014년 행사로 2016년 10월 업데이트 예정입니다. 국악과 놀아보는 한마당! 국악한마당은 국악을 통해 우리 민족 전통예술을 체험할 수 있는 공연이다. 매년 10월 개최되는 국악한마당에서는, 국악 명인공연, 세시풍속 및 전통문화 체험 프로그램, 국악 학습관 등을 통해 보고, 즐기고, 체험할 수 있는 다양한 장이 마련된다.

en.name: Seoul Gugak Festival
en.summary: Every October, the Seoul Gugak Festival offers visitors the chance to see and experience traditional Korean performing arts.
en.description: ※ This is a 2014 event. Further information about this event in 2019 will be updated at a later date. Every October, the Seoul Gugak Festival offers visitors the chance to see and experience traditional Korean performing arts. Attendees will be able to get an exquisite glimpse into Korean traditional music, song, and dance by those who have been officially designated as luminaries of the genre.

ko.name: 단오 행사
ko.summary: 올해에도 서울시 곳곳에서 단오를 맞이하여 전통문화행사가 열린다. 세시풍습 체험 등 다채로운 체험행사와 한국을 대표하는 국악신동의 공연, 퓨전국악 공연들이 펼쳐진다.
ko.description: 음력 5월 5일 인 ‘단오’는 설날과 추석에 이은 우리나라 3대 명절 중 하나이다. 모심기·씨 뿌리기가 끝나는 5월에 산의 신, 땅의 신에게 제사를 지내고 1년의 풍년을 기원하는 날이다. 또한 장마시작 전이기도 한 5월은 유행병이 돌기 쉽다고 생각해 단오에 악마를 물리치는 의미를 담아 다양한 풍습도 행해지게 되었다. 이러한 단오의 전통적인 풍습 견학과 체험을 할 수 있는 ‘단오축제’나 ‘단오제’는 매년 전국 각지에서 열려 우리나라 초여름의 풍물시가 되었다. 올해에도 서울시 곳곳에서 단오를 맞이하여 전통문화행사가 열린다. 세시풍습 체험 등 다채로운 체험행사와 먹거리를 즐겨볼 수 있다.

en.name: Dano Festival
en.summary: Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok.
en.description: Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok. The holiday originated from the Mahan Confederacy, a confederation of Korean states that existed more than 2,000 years ago. Also called Surit-nal, it is celebrated on the fifth day of the fifth month of the lunar calendar. This year it falls on Thursday, June 1. On Dano, women traditionally wash their hair in water boiled with sweet flag, and men wear iris roots around their waist. Tteok (rice cakes) made with herbs are also eaten on this day. You can experience Dano and its related customs at the Namsangol Hanok Village or at the National Folk Museum of Korea. A variety of events are scheduled, including washing hair with sweet flag, making bows, fans, and kites, tasting herb rice cakes, riding swings and more.

ko.name: 한강 역사탐방 프로그램「한강의 역사를 찾아서」
ko.summary: 서울시는 우리 민족의 젖줄인 한강의 역사를 시민들에게 알리기 위해 한강과 그 주변 역사문화유적지를 연계한 한강 역사 여행 10대 탐방코스를 4월 1일(화)부터~11월 29일(토)까지 운영한다.
ko.description: 서울시는 우리 민족의 젖줄인 한강의 역사를 시민들에게 알리기 위해 한강과 그 주변 역사문화유적지를 연계한 한강 역사 여행 10대 탐방코스를 4월 1일(화)부터~11월 29일(토)까지 운영한다. 「한강의 역사를 찾아서」는 ▲ ‘도보코스’ ▲ ‘선상코스’와 ▲ 한강역사해설사가 학교 또는 지자체에서 운영하는 단체 등에 직접 찾아가서 한강 관련 역사, 문화 및 인물에 관해 역사해설을 해주는 ‘찾아가는 역사탐방’ 등 세 개 코스로 운영된다. 프로그램 성격에 따라 개인 또는 단체 접수로 나뉘며, 예약접수는 3월 17일(월)부터 시작해 운영기간 내(4월 1일~11월 29일) 언제라도 신청이 가능하다. 개인신청은 ‘도보코스’(1코스 광나루길~9코스 겸재정선길)만 가능하며, ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램은 학교를 포함한 단체 신청, ‘선상코스(한강 옛 나루터길)’는 학교만 신청이 가능하다. 10개 코스의 평균 소요시간은 1시간~2시간 30분(선택사항)이다. ‘도보코스’와 ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램 참가를 원하는 시민들은 서울시공공서비스예약시스템( http://yeyak.seoul.go.kr )을 통해 참여희망일 10일전까지 신청하면 된다. ‘도보코스’는 월~토요일 오전 10시~오후 4시까지 진행되며, 1회 팀당 3~40명까지 가능하다. (3명 미만일 경우 프로그램이 취소됨) ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램은 월~금요일 오전 10시~오후 4시까지 진행되며, 학교 또는 노인대학 등 지자체에서 운영하는 단체 교육 프로그램을 대상으로 한다. (인원수 제한 없음) ‘선상코스(한강 옛 나루터길)’는 주 5일제 수업과 관련해 특별 기획한 청소년을 위한 프로그램으로(초·중·고등학교에서만 신청가능), 개인 신청은 불가하다. 매주 토요일 오전 10~12시까지 운영하며, 최소인원은 15명이고 최대 50명까지 가능하다.(방학기간에는 운영하지 않음) 프로그램에 참여하고 싶은 사람들은 21일전까지 한강사업본부 수상관리과로 전화신청(☎02-3780-0825)하면 된다. 전체 프로그램 관련 자세한 내용은 한강사업본부 문화홍보과(☎02-3780-0762)로 문의하면 된다.

ko.name: 꽃피는 3월, 서울시 문화예술 프로그램 안내
ko.summary: 꽁꽁 언 겨울을 지나 꽃피는 봄, 3월이 돌아왔다. 새봄을 기다렸다 활짝 피어나는 꽃망울처럼 서울의 문화예술프로그램이 쏟아진다.
ko.description: 세계인이 가장 좋아하는 화가인 빈센트 반 고흐를 재조명한 뮤지컬, <빈센트 반 고흐> 가 4월 27일까지 충무아트홀에서 펼쳐진다. ‘별이 빛나는 밤에’, ‘해바라기’ 등 고흐의 살아 숨 쉬는 그림을 3D 프로젝션 맵핑 기법을 활용해 무대 위에 펼치고, 그의 인생을 담은 음악과 함께 선보인다. 서울시립교향악단은 3월 21일 세종문화회관 체임버홀에서 <실내악 시리즈> 의 두 번째 무대로 다양한 편성의 윈드 앙상블 작품을 선보인다. 이번 무대에서 연주하는 모차르트 <세레나데 10번> ‘그랑파르티타’는 13개의 관악기와 7악장으로 구성된 대규모 실내악 작품으로 치밀하고 탄탄한 구조 속에서 다채로운 관악기의 매력을 느낄 수 있는 작품이다. <내 마음의 슈퍼맨> 은 평범하지만 위대한 영웅인 아버지에 대해서 진지하게 생각해보게 하는 작품으로 각박한 사회를 살아가는 우리들의 마음속에 뜨거운 감동을 불러일으킬 국내 초연인 연극이다. 충무아트홀에서 3월 8일부터 만날 수 있다. 노원문화예술회관에서는 3월 29일 코미디 뮤지컬 <넌센스> 가 펼쳐진다. 뮤지컬 <넌센스>는 1991년 국내 초연 이후 23년 동안 최장공연기록과 최다관객기록을 세운 최고의 히트작이다.

ko.name: 도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어
ko.summary: 한양도성 무료 해설 투어「도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어」프로그램이 3월부터 12월까지 매주 일요일(13:30∼17:00)에 진행된다. 해설은 한양도성 안내해설자원활동가인 ‘서울KYC 도성길라잡이’ 가 무료로 진행하며, 4개 코스를 주별로 돌아가면서 진행한다.
ko.description: 한양도성 무료 해설 투어「도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어」프로그램이 3월부터 12월까지 매주 일요일(13:30∼17:00)에 진행된다. 해설은 한양도성 안내해설자원활동가인 ‘서울KYC 도성길라잡이’ 가 무료로 진행하며, 4개 코스를 주별로 돌아가면서 진행한다. 4개 투어코스는 ▴1주차 ‘광희문〜숭례문’ ▴2주차 ‘숭례문〜창의문’ ▴3주차 ‘창의문〜혜화문’ ▴4주차 ‘혜화문〜광희문’으로, 소요시간은 약 3시간 30분 정도(13:30〜17:00) 소요된다. 해설이 함께하는 이번 투어의 매력은 내사산 숲길과 도심, 주택가에 남아있는 한양도성의 흔적을 만나는 데 있다. 4개 구간별로 펼쳐지는 다양한 풍경과 이야기는 600년 성곽도시 수도 서울에서만 느낄 수 있는 특별한 도보여행인 셈이다. 몸과 마음이 바쁜 도시민에게 18.6km의 한양도성 걷기는 작은 쉼과 휴식의 시간을 제공해 줄 것이다.

ko.name: The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)
ko.summary: 주한영국대사관은 영국 국가 홍보 ‘GREAT 캠페인’의 일환으로 2014년 3월 27일부터 31일까지 5일간 신사동 가로수길에서 <2014 The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)>을 진행한다.
ko.description: 주한영국대사관은 영국 국가 홍보 ‘GREAT 캠페인’의 일환으로 2014년 3월 27일부터 31일까지 5일간 신사동 가로수길에서 <2014 The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)>을 진행한다. 올해 국내에서 열리는 은 영국 주력 산업 분야인 패션, 디자인, 음식 및 주류의 우수성을 알리고자 ‘Fashion is GREAT’, ‘Creativity is GREAT’, ‘Food is GREAT’, ‘Pubs are GREAT’ 등의 주제 하에 다채로운 이벤트를 선보인다. 올 봄 서울의 가장 트렌디한 장소인 가로수길에 입점된 개성 넘치는 영국 브랜드숍의 특별 프로모션과 이벤트는 물론, 다양한 영국의 펍 문화와 음식 문화를 체험해 볼 수 있다. 이번 페스티벌에서는 신사의 나라 또는 영국 왕실등에서 비롯된 영국의 고전적인 기존 이미지를 벗은 현대적이면서 감각적인 영국 브랜드와 문화 콘텐츠를 한 곳에서 체험할 수 있게 될 것이다. 2월 마지막 주부터 페스티벌 기간(4월 첫째 주)까지 주한영국대사관 페이스북에서는 GREAT 캠페인과 페스티벌에 대한 자세한 소개 및 다양한 퀴즈, 경품 이벤트를 진행한다. GREAT 캠페인은 영국의 다채로운 문화와 산업을 홍보하고, 비즈니스 파트너로서의 영국의 이미지를 제고하며, 국제적인 관심을 도모하기 위해 3년째 진행되고 있다.

en.name: The GREAT Campaign
en.summary: Organized by the British Embassy in Seoul, the 'GREAT Campaign' will showcase the best of Britian's creativity, technology, culture, and food.
en.description: Organized by the British Embassy in Seoul, the 'GREAT Campaign' will showcase the best of Britian's creativity, technology, culture, and food. From March 27 to March 31, Garosu-gil in Seoul will become a full-fledged British cultural destination. Pub crawl through some of the British themed pop-up pubs for some tasty food, beer and gin; shop at British brand shops, and participate in various events for awesome prizes. Don't miss the chance to experience the best of GREAT Britain right here in Seoul. Britain is one of the leading destinations for the fashion industry, renowned for its trendsetting, uniqueness, and creativity. Enjoy the best of British fashion in Seoul! Travis, a popular British alternative rock band will return to Korea with their latest album 'Where you stand' on March 25, 2014 at the Olympic Hall in Seoul. Tickets are available at ticket.interpark.com Enjoy the best British foods and drinks at cafés and bars around Garosu-gil. Find out more and participate in various events and quizzes at the British Embassy Seoul Facebook page ( https://www.facebook.com/ukinrok )

ko.name: 매달 마지막 수요일, 문화가 있는 날
ko.summary: 2014년 1월부터 매월 마지막 수요일이 ‘문화가 있는 날’로 정해졌다. 문화가 있는 날에는 관람료 무료•할인 혜택이 제공되고, 야간개방 및 문화프로그램 등이 확대 시행된다.
ko.description: 2014년 1월부터 매월 마지막 수요일이 ‘문화가 있는 날’로 정해졌다. 문화가 있는 날에는 관람료 무료•할인 혜택이 제공되고, 야간개방 및 문화프로그램 등이 확대 시행된다. ‘문화가 있는 날’에는 유료로 운영 중이던 국•공•사립 전시 관람시설은 물론, 많은 국민이 즐기는 영화, 프로스포츠와 관람료가 다소 부담이 되던 공연프로그램도 대폭 할인된 가격에 즐길 수 있다. 또한, 국공립 박물관•미술관, 도서관은 야간개방도 실시한다.

en.name: Culture Day - Last Weds of Every Month
en.summary: The last Wednesday of each month in 2014 has been designated as a special "Culture Day" in Korea.
en.description: The last Wednesday of each month in 2014 has been designated as a special "Culture Day" in Korea. During culture day, participating museums, galleries and other cultural facilities will offer free or discounted admission. The royal palaces, Jongmyo Shrine, the National Theater of Korea, National Gugak Center, Korea National Opera, and Korean National Ballet are just a few of the many participants of Korea's Culture Day.

ko.name: 운현궁 궁중의상체험
ko.summary: 운현궁에서 매일(월요일 제외) 궁중의상체험 행사를 진행하고 있다. 의상을 직접 입어보고 운현궁을 거닐며 자유롭게 촬영 가능하다.
ko.description: 운현궁에서 매일(월요일 제외) 궁중의상체험 행사를 진행하고 있다. 의상을 직접 입어보고 운현궁을 거닐며 자유롭게 촬영 가능하다.

en.name: Unhyeongung Palace Royal Costume Experience
en.summary: Unhyeongung Palace offers a cultural experience program where tourists and residents can try on royal costume attire. Royal costumes may be rented for an hour at a time and may be worn while touring the royal palace and/or for taking photos.

ko.name: 조선시대 과거제 행사
ko.summary: 1994년 서울정도 600년 기념행사로 시작하여 올해 21회를 맞이하는 ‘조선시대 과거제 재현행사’는 경희궁에서 한시 백일장 형태로 진행되며, 국왕(뮤지컬배우 남경주 특별출연)이 내린 어사화를 쓰고 행진하는 ‘유가행렬(遊街行列)’이 행사의 마지막을 장식할 것이다.
ko.description: 1994년 서울정도 600년 기념행사로 시작하여 올해 21회를 맞이하는 ‘조선시대 과거제 재현행사’는 공정경쟁을 통해 인재를 뽑는 선진적 제도이자 세계적으로 빛나는 한민족의 문화유산인 과거제를 널리 알리고, 시민들에게 우리 전통문화의 우수성을 되새길 수 있는 계기를 마련할 것이다. ‘조선시대 과거제 재현행사’는 한시 백일장 형태로 진행되며, 세종실록오례의 가례 문과전시의를 토대로 원형에 따라 실시된다. 과거시험 후에는 급제자를 발표하는 방방례(放榜禮), 급제를 축하하는 은영연(恩榮宴)이 경희궁 과장에서 재현되며, 급제자가 국왕(뮤지컬배우 남경주 특별출연)이 내린 어사화를 쓰고 행진하는 ‘유가행렬(遊街行列)’이 행사의 마지막을 장식할 것이다. <2014년도 제 21회 조선시대 과거제 재현행사 과시생 모집> - 일시: 2014. 10. 5(일) 10:30~17:00 - 장소: 경희궁 - 모집인원: 선착순 200명 - 응시자격: 제한없음(전국)/ ※단 1회~20회 장원급자는 제외 - 시험내용: 한시(漢詩_七言律學) - 접수기간: 2014. 9. 12(금)~10. 2(목)/ ※신청기간 중 응시인원 접수 초과 시 해당일 접수분까지만 인정 - 접수 방법: 직접방문, 우편, 인터넷 접수/ ※과거제 행사 당일 현장접수 불가, 반드시 접수기한내 가급적 인터넷 접수 바람

ko.name: 덕수궁 왕궁수문장 교대의식
ko.summary: 왕궁수문장 교대의식은 조선시대 왕궁에는 수문군이라는 군대가 있어 궁궐 문을 개폐, 경비, 순찰하는 업무 등을 수행하였다. 왕궁 수문장 교대의식은 영국 왕실의 근위병 교대의식과 비견되는 화려하고 품위 있는 한국전통 궁중 문화 재현행사이다.
ko.description: 교대를 앞둔 두 무리의 수문군이 대한문 앞에서 마주한다. 카메라나 캠코더로 장면을 담기에 여념이 없는 외국인 관광객도 많다. 북소리가 울리기 전부터 덕수궁 대한문 앞 광장은 왕궁수문장 교대의식을 보기 위해 모여든 사람으로 가득하다. 수문군을 빙 둘러 포위한 형세다. 엄고수(북을 치는 이)의 힘찬 손동작이 허공을 가른다. 둥! 둥! 둥! 세 번의 북소리. 수문장 교대의식을 알리는 개식 타고다. 수문장의 인솔 아래 궁 주변을 순찰하던 교대군이 궁성문에 도착한다. 의식을 위한 모든 준비를 완료한다. 엄고의 북소리가 울린다. 두 수문군의 가운데로 감독관에 해당하는 녹색 단령 차림의 승정원 주서와 궁성의 기물과 열쇠를 관장하는 액정서 소속의 사약이 나온다. ‘군호 응대!’ 하는 힘찬 울림이 퍼지면 양군의 참사가 군호를 확인한다. 군호는 서로의 신원을 확인하는 일종의 암호다. 병조에서 세 글자 이내로 국왕께 보고하면 승정원을 통해 내려온다. 승정원 주서가 동참하는 이유다. 승정원 주서가 수문장과 수문군에게 군호를 알려준다. 일말의 긴장감이 맴돌면서 관람객들이 의식의 절도를 느끼는 순간이다. 이어 ‘초엄’ 하는 참하의 외침에 따라 수문군들이 ‘초엄’을 복창하고 다음 의식이 이뤄진다. 교대의식의 첫 번째 절차를 알리는 신호로 나각과 나발 소리가 여섯 번 울린다. 주위를 환기시키는 신호다. 관람객들은 숨을 죽인 채 그들의 동작 하나하나를 지켜본다. 수문군과 관람객 사이에 따로 구분선이 있는 것은 아니다. 군악을 담당하는 취라척과 관람객은 최소한의 걸음만을 유지한 채 자리한다. 숨소리까지 다 들릴 만큼 가까운 거리다. 궁성문의 열쇠가 들어 있는 약시함의 인계가 이뤄지며 본격적인 수문장 교대의식에 들어간다. 수문군의 참하가 수문장에게 약시함을 전달하는데, 약시함에는 궁성문의 열쇠가 들어 있다. 열쇠가 가지는 상징성은 의식에도 고스란히 스며든다. 이 과정을 승정원 주서와 액정서 사약이 지켜본다. 개개의 동작은 유연하지만 절도 있다. 영국의 근위병 교대의식과 비교하자면 부드러움 속에 격식의 꼿꼿함을 숨기고 있다. 보는 이들도 좀 더 쉽게 다가선다. 참하의‘중엄’ 하는 외침과 수문군들의 복창, 드디어 교대 의식의 두 번째 절차가 시작된다. 이를 알리는 나각과 나발 소리가 세 번 엄고를 울리면 양 수문장들이 인사 후 부신을 맞추고 순장패를 인수인계한다. 부신은 두 조각으로 나뉜 나뭇조각인데 둘이 이빨을 맞춰 한 짝을 이룬다. 일종의 신분 확인서다. 마지막 절차는 ‘삼엄’이다. ‘향전’이라는 외침에 따라 수문군들이 자리를 이동해 얼굴을 마주하는 ‘면간’ 교대의식을 치른다. 수문장들에 이은 수문군간의 교대의식이다. 마지막으로 참하가 한 번 더 ‘향전’이라고 외치면 모든 절차가 끝난다. 교대를 마친 수문군은 숭례문까지 순라를 한다. 교대의식은 총 20분 정도 소요된다. 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않아 지나가던 행인도 걸음을 멈추곤 한다. 이제는 서울에서 빼놓을 수 없는 의식으로 서울 시민들에게 많은 사랑을 받고 있다.

en.name: Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung Palace
en.summary: The Changing of the Royal Guard is a re-enactment of the ceremony from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) for changing the guards that protected and patrolled the royal palaces, and were in charge of the opening and closing of the gates to the palaces.
en.description: During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guards were responsible for guarding and patrolling the gates of the capital city and the royal palaces. The royal palace guards, who were known as the "Wanggung Sumunjang", had the very important duty of protecting the king by guarding the entrance gates of the primary royal palace where the king resided. They were in charge of opening and closing the palace gates, inspecting all visitors, and maintaining a close surveillance of the palace. They were divided into day and night shifts, and the Changing of the Guard ceremony took place whenever the shifts changed over. In the late period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Changing of the Guard ceremony was conducted at Deoksugung Palace as at that time Deoksugung was the primary royal palace and the king then resided there. The Changing of the Guard ceremony was originally conducted at Gyeongbokgung Palace in the early Joseon period, but was moved to Deoksugung when Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace after Gyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Invasions of 1592 - 1598. After some extensive historical research, this splendid and elegant traditional Korean royal court cultural ceremony was first re-enacted in 1996 and has been a must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions ever since. This ceremony is a great opportunity to experience a rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments. A tradition comparable to the Changing of the Guards at Buckingham Palace, this ceremony takes place three times a day in front of Daehanmun, the main gate of Deoksugung at 11:00, 14:00, and 15:30 p.m. (except for on Mondays). The Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung starts with two mounted soldiers leading the way, and a total of 78 Sumungun making an appearance, led by the Sumunjang in the order of Sumunjang, Sumungun, Sungjeongwon Juseo, Aekjeongseo Sayak and Chwiracheok. Once all the Sumungun have arrived with the drumbeat of the Chwiracheok (a military band), it marks the beginning of the changing ceremony.

ko.name: 소극장 산울림
ko.summary: <고도를 기다리며>로 유명한 한국 공연문화예술의 메카
ko.description: 1969년 창단된 극단 산울림은 사무엘 베케트의 <고도를 기다리며>를 한국 초연을 시작으로 한국을 대표하는 극단으로 성장했으며, 1985년 전용 극장인 ‘소극장 산울림’을 개관하였습니다. 이곳은 고전극은 물론 실험적인 현대극 등 수많은 작품을 무대에 올리며 현대 연극의 새로운 역사를 썼습니다. <위기의 여자>, <엄마는 오십에 바다를 발견했다> 등 사회에 큰 울림을 준 여성 연극을 탄생시킨 곳입니다. 1층엔 ‘산울림 아트 앤 크래프트’라는 갤러리&아트샵을 함께 운영 중입니다.

en.name: Theater Sanwoollim
en.summary: Cultural capital of Korea, famous for Waiting for Godot
en.description: Founded in 1969, the theater company has grown to become one of Korea's leading theater companies, starting with the Korean premiere of Samuel Beckett's <Waiting for Godot>, and in 1985, it opened its own theater, the Small Theater Sanulim. The company has written a new history of contemporary theater by staging numerous works, including classical plays as well as experimental contemporary plays. It is the birthplace of women's plays that resonated with society, such as <Woman in Crisis> and <My Mother Found the Sea at Fifty>. The theater also operates a gallery and art shop called 'Sanwoollim Art & Craft' on the first floor.

en.name: Hangang Art Park
en.summary: A beautiful interactive park and resting area for visitors to enjoy up to 37 different public art works that put an artistic spin on the Hangang River from a cultural arts perspective. Stop on by for some personal healing amid the cold, bustling life of the city in this beautifully imaginative park dedicated to the arts filled with inspiration, wonder, and enjoyment.
en.description: Breaking away from the common idea that the Hangang River serves as simply a place of leisure and picnicking, the Hangang Art Park aims to present the river in a much different light. Guided by the philosophy, "Hangang, art in the flow," the park seeks to create a Hangang River that gently flows along its course at the hands of artistry. In other words, the goal is to advocate the rebirth of the Hangang River park area as a place of thoughtful communication and exchange, in line with the concept of a more stimulating and impactful form of leisure that naturally melds with the "stop" and "flow" of the river body itself. The artwork found at the park was selected through a series of art competitions that featured both professional artists and artists among the public. An artwork selection committee, comprised of specialists from a variety of fields, then worked faithfully to develop and promote the chosen artwork, which the committee had selected on the basis of not only the representation of geographical characteristics, but also substance and diversity. It was through this process of selection that the artwork currently on display was chosen, all of which belong to one of the four specified themes of the park: "Lively," "Relaxed," "Inspiring," and "Secretive."

en.name: Haebangchon Alleyway
en.summary: Literally meaning "liberated village", Haebangchon is a popular attraction that was once made up of empty market spaces and alleyways before it underwent urban regeneration.
en.description: Literally meaning "liberated village", Haebangchon is a popular attraction that was once made up of empty market spaces and alleyways before it underwent urban regeneration. Connected to Namsan Mountain, the upper areas of this sloped village are hard to reach but worth the climb for its beautiful panoramic views. It is frequently visited not only by tourists and travelers, but also old residents and people from all walks of life. As Itaewon became popular in the mid-2000s, Haebangchon also started gaining attention from people passing by. Because of the gentrification of Gangnam, Hongdae, and Itaewon, Haebangchon began to transform into a gathering place for aspiring young artists and creators. The area is full of unique little workshops, cafes, and bookstores. Meanwhile, cafes and restaurant with a more sophisticated atmosphere have been appearing near the street of Sinheung-ro, continuing to bring in many more visitors to the area.

en.name: Digital Media City
en.summary: Digital Media City is located in Sangam-dong and was purpose-built to house Korea's media, entertainment, and the IT industries with the aim of becoming the new epicenter for Hallyu content and production.
en.description: Digital Media City (DMC) is an IT and media industry cluster located in Mapo-gu, housing numerous headquarters of major domestic corporations. Currently, it hosts the three major terrestrial broadcasters KBS, MBC, and SBS, along with cable channels like YTN, Channel A, and JTBC, and newspapers such as Dong-A Ilbo and JoongAng Ilbo. Additionally, the Korean Film Archive, the nation's only film archive equipped with Korean movie films and related materials, is located there. This makes DMC a hub for the production of Hallyu content. Furthermore, the area is surrounded by various renowned restaurants, making it a recommended tourist destination for those interested in K-media.

en.name: The Story of King Sejong • The Story of Admiral Yi Sunshin
en.summary: The Story of King Sejong and The Story of Admiral Yi Sunshin are exhibitions halls about two of Korea's national heroes, King Sejong and Admiral Yi.
en.description: The Story of King Sejong and The Story of Admiral Yi Sunshin are exhibitions halls about two of Korea's national heroes, King Sejong and Admiral Yi. The exhibition halls are located on the B2 level of the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts. In addition to viewing the exhibitions, children can also experience traditional Korean culture and try on hanbok. For more information on these activities, please ask at the information desk.

en.name: Hangdong Railroad
en.summary: Located in Guro-gu, Hangdong Railroad is a popular attraction for pedestrians.
en.description: 구로구에 위치한 항동철길은 소박한 기찻길과 아름다운 자연 덕분에 서울 최고의 산책 명소입니다. 서울의 다른 어떤 곳과도 비교할 수 없는 독특한 기찻길 풍경과 푸른 수목원으로 이어지는 아름다운 산책로를 자랑합니다. 연인과의 산책이나 가족 나들이에 최적의 장소로 널리 알려지고 있습니다.

en.name: Hwarang-ro: Fallen Leaves Street
en.summary: Hwarang-ro is a street in northern Seoul, stretching from Taereung Royal Tomb to the Samyuk-daero area, and is most known for its beautiful, scenic foliage during the autumn season.
en.description: Hwarang-ro is a street in Northern Seoul that is famous for its autumn foliage and fallen leaves. Hwarang-ro run 8.6 km from Taereung to Sahmyook University. Fallen leaves are not swept away and they're left for a short period of time so that walkers and visitors can appreciate the autumn colors and ambience. The street has been selected as the best autumn color and foliage street in Seoul.

en.name: Ahwon Workshop
en.summary: A metal craft store that offers both gallery exhibitions and goods on display
en.description: Awon Gongbang was first opened in 1983 in an alley in Insadong by metalworking sisters Noh Inah and Noh injung, and now operates stores and galleries in Samcheong-dong and Sunra-gil. They handcraft and sell metal-based crafts such as candlesticks, vases, mobiles, and necklaces, and the shop also features works by craft artists in various fields such as glass, ceramics, textiles, and woodworking. The basement is home to a permanent exhibition of Noh's work, jewelry from Aowon Workshop, and other artists' work, and there is a cafe on the third floor.

en.name: Hoegi-dong Annyeong Village
en.summary: Annyeong Village, where variously colored mural paintings warmly welcomes you
en.description: Annyeong village is where everyone works hard for a safe and joyful village by greeting and welcoming each other. The murals painted throughout the streets soften the atmosphere of the town. Let’s head to Annyeong Village to check out the colorful murals.

en.name: Woori-jip Guesthouse
en.summary: Experience the beauty of traditional architecture with a stay at the Woori-jip Guesthouse in Bukchon Hanok Village.
en.description: Experience the beauty of traditional architecture with a stay at the Woori-jip Guesthouse in Bukchon Hanok Village. The guesthouse is popular as a unique accommodation in Seoul, and as a regular tourist attraction. The guesthouse often hosts concertsandparties that are popular with locals, expats, and tourists alike.

en.name: LuggageQ Hongdae Branch
en.summary: A 24-hour unmanned luggage storage near Hongik University Station where you can affordably store your items in large lockers that can fit up to six 20-inch suitcases.
en.description: We conveniently store the heavy luggage of travelers near Hongik University Station. With large lockers that can fit up to six 20-inch suitcases, you can store various items like suitcases and shopping bags amply all at once, and enjoy your trip to Seoul more lightly with our 24-hour unmanned operation.

en.name: LuggageQ Seoul Station Branch
en.summary: A 24-hour unmanned luggage storage near Seoul Station where you can affordably store your items in large lockers that can fit up to six 20-inch suitcases.
en.description: We conveniently store the heavy luggage of travelers near Seoul Station. With large lockers that can fit up to six 20-inch suitcases, you can store various items like suitcases and shopping bags amply all at once, and enjoy your trip to Seoul more lightly with our 24-hour unmanned operation.

en.name: Yongsan Cultural Foundation Complex Cultural Space
en.summary: A central hub for culture and arts integrated into daily life.
en.description: The Yongsan Cultural Foundation Complex Cultural Space serves as a strategic creative anchor in Yongsan, linking the neighborhoods of Hangangjin and Itaewon. Functioning as a versatile multi-purpose facility, it accommodates an array of activities—including exhibitions, performances, content production, creative support, and pop-up cultural events—aiming to operate as an open cultural platform connecting citizens, artists, and local resources.

en.name: Hangangjin Station
en.summary: The start of Hannam-dong's hidden showroom street, a Line 6 subway station you want to walk along.
en.description: Hangangjin Station is a station flanked above and below by Seoul attractions like Itaewon and Noksapyeong Station. Nearby, attractions and cultural facilities such as Comme des Garçons Street, Leeum Museum of Art, and Blue Square are located. Close to the Namsan walking trail and situated in a luxurious residential area, you can feel a sense of tranquility while enjoying the charm where main boulevards and alleys coexist.

en.name: Hangang Play Place
en.summary: A complex cultural space where all the joys of the Han River come together, offering diverse ways to experience the many charms of the Han River.
en.description: Hangang Play Place is a complex cultural space where the diverse attractions of the Han River can be experienced in one place. The name Hangang Play Place is an abbreviation of Play and Place, carrying the meaning of adding imagination and fun to the Han River, and inviting visitors to experience the Han River we love in a new way. From various hands on programs and performances to media art, rest lounges, and an otter playground, this space is designed as a new Han River themed park that all generations from children to adults can enjoy together. A special cultural resting space where the charm of the Han River can be felt in many ways, Hangang Play Place invites you to discover a new everyday life along the Han River.
en.address: Ttukseom Jabeolle Building, First Floor, 2202 Gangbyeonbuk ro, Gwangjin gu, Seoul
en.hours:
Weekdays 10:00 to 19:00
Weekends and Public Holidays 10:00 to 20:00

en.name: Arcade Seoul
en.summary: A Mullae dong complex cultural space born from an old iron workshop
en.description: Opened in 2023, Arcade Seoul is a complex cultural space in Mullae dong that remodeled a building previously used as an iron workshop and presents diverse content across genres such as exhibitions, pop ups, performances, and talk shows. Arcade Seoul first opened in Hongdae as a complex cultural space with content including a fashion select shop and exhibition space. The newly introduced Arcade Seoul Mullae branch operates as a space more specialized in content such as pop ups and exhibitions, serving as another urban walking destination for city dwellers.
en.address: First floor, 23 Dorim ro 128 gil, Yeongdeungpo gu, Seoul

en.name: Chungmuro Station
en.summary: A station located in Chungmuro, once called the mecca of Korean cinema.
en.description: Chungmuro Station is a transfer station for Subway Line 3 and Subway Line 4. Since the 1950s, Chungmuro had been known as the mecca of Korean cinema due to the concentration of film production companies and theaters. Although the old theaters have gradually disappeared into history and the Chungmuro era has faded, its proximity to Myeongdong and Euljiro, which are visited frequently by young people and foreign visitors, is giving new life to the area once shaped by the film industry. With the harmony of traditional shops and new establishments, Chungmuro is now frequented not only by the middle aged but also by the younger generation.

en.name: Magok Cultural Street
en.summary: A cultural and artistic street in Magok District
en.description: Magok Cultural Street, located in the heart of the Magok district, is a multi-purpose cultural space featuring busking stages for performances, diverse public art installations, and media art. It provides vitality to both locals and visitors. Seasonal street performances, festivals, and outdoor exhibitions are popular highlights, and visitors can also enjoy nearby cafés and restaurants.

en.name: Seoul Regional Tourism Center
en.summary: A space where you can discover travel information from all regions of Korea in one place
en.description: The Seoul Regional Tourism Center provides both visitors to Seoul and local citizens with opportunities to view and experience exhibitions of regional tourism content. This initiative is promoted as part of a project to foster coexistence between Seoul and other regions and has been created as a hub that connects tourism in Seoul with that of other regions.Visitors can experience contents related to tourism in 10 regions, including Gangwon, Gyeongbuk, Daejeon, Andong, Jeonnam, Jeju, Chungnam, Chungcheongbuk-do, Tongyeong, and Hadong, using various senses such as sight, touch, and hearing, and can also purchase representative products and goods from the regions. Exhibition content is provided in both Korean and English, and visitors can also obtain regional maps and brochures offered by each area.

en.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley
en.summary: The food alley of Euljiro
en.description: Euljiro Nogari Alley grew rapidly in popularity during the IMF economic crisis, becoming a hotspot for a unique Korean drinking culture centered on nogari (dried pollack) and beer. In the evenings, the alley is crowded to the extent that even outdoor tables have no vacancies, making it one of Euljiro’s oldest and most beloved food alleys.

en.name: Tongui-dong Alley
en.summary: An alley located west of Gyeongbokgung Palace, where historical value is preserved
en.description: This alley, located west of Gyeongbokgung Palace, preserves historical value as a site related to Gyeomjae Jeong Seon and Chusa Kim Jeong-hui, where logistics movement and human exchange for Gyeongbokgung Palace were once active. During the Joseon Dynasty, great artists like Gyeomjae Jeong Seon and Chusa Kim Jeong-hui resided in Seochon. In modern times, notable artists, including painters Lee Jung-seop and Lee Sang-beom, and poets Yun Dong-ju and Yi Sang, were also residents. We hope you will enjoy exploring history and culture together in Tongui-dong Alley, where a cultural village has been established with various cultural and artistic spaces, such as the Boan Inn, where poets Yi Sang, Yun Dong-ju, and painter Lee Jung-seop once stayed.

en.name: COEX K-POP Square
en.summary: A landmark destination with giant outdoor screens reminiscent of Times Square
en.description: 코엑스 아티움 의 거대한 LED 미디어 파사드 바로 아래에 위치한 코엑스 K-팝 스퀘어는 삼성역 , 스타필드 코엑스 몰, 현대 백화점 과 인접한 활기 넘치는 공공 광장 입니다 . 이곳은 마치 파도 가 스크린 을 뚫고 들어오는 듯한 놀라운 효과 를 연출 하는 3D 착시 예술 작품 '웨이브(WAVE)'가 설치된 대형 스마트 LED 디스플레이 로 유명 합니다 . K- 팝 과 한류 콘텐츠 가 끊임없이 상영 되는 코엑스 K- 팝 스퀘어 는 서울 최고의 디지털 미디어 랜드 마크 로서 관광객 과 현지인 모두 에게 사랑 받고 있습니다 . 서울 곳곳에 3D 디지털 사이니지가 설치 되고 있지만 , 코엑스 K- 팝 스퀘어 는 그중에서도 가장 상징 적이고 영향력 있는 곳 으로 자리 매김하고 있습니다 .

en.name: Nowon Dumulmaru
en.summary: A space with great views located at the confluence of Jungnangcheon and Danghyeoncheon
en.description: This is a cafe and rest area located at the confluence of Jungnangcheon and Danghyeoncheon, which you can encounter while walking along Jungnang Dulle-gil. At the store, you can enjoy Han River ramyeon, cooked with instant cookers just like at the Han River, and appreciate the natural scenery from the observatory built in the rest area. Nowon Dumulmaru is beloved as a healing walking destination for nearby residents. We recommend taking a brief rest with a cup of tea while looking out at Jungnangcheon.

en.name: OPCD Vinyl LP Library
en.summary: A cultural space for listening to music through vinyl records
en.description: OPCD (Open Chang-dong) is a music creation support platform based in Chang-dong, the future site of the Seoul Arena scheduled for completion in 2027. It runs various creative support projects in collaboration with professional musicians and emerging artists. Just outside Exit 1 of Chang-dong Station, you will find a unique space built under the subway overpass. Here, the OPCD Vinyl LP Library offers a welcoming, open area where you can enjoy vinyl record music for free. This is a recommended stop for anyone interested in analog music experiences.
en.hours: Monday to Friday 12:00 to 20:00, Saturday and Sunday 12:00 to 18:00

en.name: Hongdae R2 Busking Street
en.summary: A walkable street filled with various busking performances
en.description: The R2 area, known as the “Street You Want to Walk,” is a pedestrian-friendly street where a wide range of busking performances take place. Performances span multiple genres including pop music, dance, magic, and mime, and are conducted through a prior registration system. During peak tourist seasons in spring and fall, visitors can also enjoy traditional cultural experiences through the “Welcome Event for Tourists.”

en.name: Little China Town
en.summary: The Chinatown centered around the Chinese Embassy located in Myeongdong.
en.description: Little China Town, the Chinatown in Myeongdong, centers around the Chinese Embassy and has been home to Chinese cuisine restaurants, Chinese elementary schools, and Chinese culture for over 100 years. It is considered the oldest Chinatown in South Korea. The Seoul Overseas Chinese School, located next to the Seoul Central Post Office, has been there since 1909, along with some imported bookstores, Chinese food specialty stores, Chinese product specialty stores, and currency exchange shops. The Hansung Chinese Association handles various tasks such as issuing and processing documents for the Chinese community. This Chinatown developed naturally and is not managed comprehensively. It is one of the places where you can feel an exotic atmosphere in the city.

en.name: Jeong-dong Observatory
en.summary: A place where you can take in a panoramic view of the heart of Seoul
en.description: Jeong-dong Observatory is located on the 13th floor of the Seosomun Building at Seoul City Hall. Inside the observatory, there is a cafe where you can enjoy beverages while taking in a view of the Deoksugung Palace area. Photos depicting the old appearance of Jeongdong are displayed on the cafe walls, allowing visitors to appreciate the historical aspect of the area. There are bar tables by the windows, providing a perfect spot to admire the stunning view while spending time, and there are also group seats, making it ideal for visiting with friends or colleagues. On clear days, you can see Gwanghwamun and the Blue House from the window seats, which are always popular. The cafe at the observatory offers not only coffee but also a variety of drinks like aids and teas at relatively affordable prices, making it a popular spot for many visitors.

en.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bukhansan Mountain)
en.summary: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bukhansan Mountain) is a 5-minute walk from Exit 2 of Bukhansan Ui Station. It offers hiking course information in multiple languages.
en.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center is just a 5-minute walk from Exit 2 of Bukhansan Ui Station and offers tourists various hiking services. Focused on Bukhansan Mountain, it provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for different hiking trails in Seoul, including Bugaksan Mountain, Inwangsan Mountain, and Gwanaksan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers free and paid lockers for convenient storage of belongings. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

en.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain)
en.summary: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain) is located in the cultural street of Samcheong-dong. It provides information on Seoul's hiking trails in multiple languages.
en.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain) is located on Samcheong-dong Cultural Street and offers a range of services for hiking tourists. Focused on Bugaksan Mountain, it provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for different hiking trails in Seoul, including Bukhansan Mountain, Inwangsan Mountain, and Gwanaksan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers free and paid lockers for convenient storage of belongings. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

en.name: Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Gwanaksan Mountain)
en.summary: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Gwanaksan Mountain) is located within Gwanaksan Station on the Sillim Line. It provides information on Seoul's hiking trails in multiple languages.
en.description: The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Gwanaksan Mountain), located within Gwanaksan Station on the Sillim Line, provides various services for hiking enthusiasts. It focuses on Gwanaksan Mountain and provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for hiking trails in Seoul, including Bukhansan Mountain, Bugaksan Mountain, and Inwangsan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. In addition to offering themed hiking experience programs for foreigners, the center provides rental services for hiking gear, such as shoes, clothing, trekking poles, gloves, and crampons (available to local visitors accompanying foreigners as well). The center also offers lockers for storage upon the use of the gear rental service at no extra cost. In the lounge, visitors can relax or create lasting memories with friends, family, or companions.

en.name: YDP CULTURAL LOUNGE DADADA
en.summary: DADADA, a cultural space in the city where everyday life meets vibrant culture and content.
en.description: Located in the plaza of Yeongdeungpo Times Square, "DADADA" is a lively cultural lounge that serves as a dynamic hub for residents and visitors. Offering various cultural events and programs, it captures the playful spirit of children who once filled the neighborhood with cheerful trumpet sounds. "DADADA" aims to infuse Yeongdeungpo with vitality by sharing diverse voices and stories. The space hosts everything from exhibitions and workshops to immersive media art experiences, positioning itself as a hub for art and creative expression. Through collaborations with local artists and the community, it organizes engaging events in a modern, thoughtfully designed space that also invites relaxation. With its welcoming atmosphere, "DADADA" provides a place where people of all ages can connect, communicate, and participate in rich cultural exchanges.

en.name: Seongsu Pedestrian Overpass
en.summary: A place where you can enjoy a wonderful sunset and night view in Seongsu
en.description: Seongsu-dong offers fantastic spots to take in Seoul’s breathtaking sunsets and night views. As the golden hour nears, photography enthusiasts gather with their cameras in hand. You can capture iconic landmarks from the bridge, such as the Hangang River, Namsan Tower, Seongsudaegyo Bridge, Seongdong-gu, and even Hannam-dong in Yongsan-gu. On the opposite side of the Namsan view, Lotte World Tower glows in soft pink hues. If you head down below the pedestrian bridge, you’ll find Hangang River Park, a perfect spot to relax while watching the sunset reflect off the river. Plan to arrive at least 30 minutes before sunset to catch the best sunset views.

en.name: Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education Namsan Library
en.summary: Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library
en.description: Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library, originally opened in 1922 as the Gyeongseong Municipal Library in Myeong-dong. Situated in the heart of Namsan, the current building was constructed in 1965 following a public design competition. It has since been recognized as a Seoul Future Heritage building. The library boasts a collection of invaluable resources, including three volumes designated as Seoul City Tangible Cultural Properties and 227 volumes of 30 registered cultural properties. With a collection of around 500,000 books, 16,000 non-book materials, and 800 serial publications, Namsan Public Library is committed to preserving and sharing knowledge. In collaboration with the National Library of Korea, it has created a digital archive of rare and valuable materials, including ancient books and East Asian texts. Additionally, the library serves as a specialized resource center for Seoul's residents, offering various programs designed to enrich their cultural and intellectual lives.

en.name: Myeongdong Jaemi-ro
en.summary: It refers to the 500m hilly road from Exit 3 of Myeongdong Station to Seoul Animation Center
en.description: Jaemi-ro is a comic street located in Myeongdong, Jung-gu. It is a content-specialized street within Sangsang Town's cultural content clustering, centered around the former Seoul Animation Center (currently undergoing reconstruction). It's a themed street stretching approximately 450m from Exit 3 of Myeongdong Station to the former Seoul Animation Center, adorned with Korean comics, animations, characters, illustrations, and other content. Jaemi-ro, connecting the iconic tourist spots of Seoul, Myeongdong, and Namsan Mountain, offers a valuable experience where visitors can enjoy diverse cultural experiences within the heart of Seoul's downtown area.
en.address: 24, Toegye-ro 20-gil, Jung-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea

en.name: Changsin-Sungin Quarry Observatory
en.summary: In the era of Japanese colonial rule, the Changsin-dong quarry was active, and atop its peak lies an observation deck, offering breathtaking night views.
en.description: The quarry observatory is built atop the summit of Changsin-dong quarry, providing a panoramic view of the city and natural landscapes at a glance. During the Japanese colonial period, a quarry was located in Naksan, Changsin-dong, to supply stone for the exterior of large buildings such as the Government-General of Korea, the old Seoul Station, and the Bank of Korea. After the Korean War, the quarry's use was discontinued, but the quarry observatory was located where immigrants and refugees settled to form a village. From the quarry observatory, with nothing obstructing the view, you can enjoy the skyline of Seoul at a glance. The second floor houses a coffee shop (Café Nakta), and the third floor features an outdoor observation deck, allowing you to appreciate the scenery of Seoul's cityscape and nature from any vantage point. Especially renowned is the breathtaking view that unfolds alongside the sunset. Enjoy the best panoramic view, a reasonably priced cup of coffee, and homemade ggangjeong and Nakta rice cakes. Small music concerts featuring historical and cultural stories, exhibitions, and live guitar performances are held occasionally.

en.name: Changsin-dong's Cliff Village
en.summary: A village built around a rock cliff used as Korea's only quarry
en.description: Changsin-dong Cliff Village, located in Changsin 1, 2, and 3-dong in Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, has undergone various transformations over the years. It was a quarry village in the 1960s, a wooden village in the 1970s, a sewing factory in the 1990s, and finally a sewing village in the 2000s. It is situated around the rocky cliffs once used as the nation's only quarry. Changsin-dong Cliff Village is divided into densely packed, dilapidated, aged homes built on cliffs and precipices and homes formed beneath rocky hills. *Please Note: When visiting, please refrain from making excessive noise, as actual residents live there.

en.name: Ihwa Mural Village
en.summary: The Ihwa Mural Village has various murals hidden in its alleys. Capture moments alongside the murals through photographs.
en.description: Below Naksan Fortress, Ihwa-dong, once a quiet neighborhood, transformed into a mural village after the 'Naksan Project.' With murals painted throughout the alleyways, have fun searching for them as you explore the village. As you climb the stairs, don't forget to turn around and enjoy the panoramic view of Seoul.

en.name: Bulgwang Blacksmith Workshop
en.summary: An old blacksmith shop with a 50 years of history, tradition, and memories
en.description: This blacksmith shop is run by two generations, father and son, and the first owner, Mr. Park Kyung-won, has been a blacksmith for over 60 years. His son, Park Sang-bum, has been a blacksmith for 26 years, and they work together to keep Bulgwang Blacksmith Shop running. All the tools made at Bulgwang Blacksmith Shop are handmade and differentiated from those made in factories. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

en.name: LCDC SEOUL
en.summary: Full of Stories of the Neighborhood, its Brands, and People LCDC SEOUL
en.description: LCDC SEOUL was built where anauto repair shop and a shoe manufacturing factory once existed. A building wasadded to the existing two factory buildings to recreate the space into a culturecomplex. It's hard to find any traces of the old auto shop, but the dark grayconcrete walls wrapping around LCDC SEOUL still blend seamlessly into thesurrounding industrial landscape. You start the morning with asweet dessert and cup of tea in the first floor cafe, move up to the second andthird floor for different cultural experiences, and reach the bar on the fourthfloor around sundown for a drink. There is no need to move to another locationsince there is plenty to do all day in this truly cultural space.

en.name: Yangcheon Park Book Shelter
en.summary: A Shelter with Nature and Book, Yangcheon Park Book Shelter
en.description: At one side of Yangcheon Park, where an energy of people doing exercise and freeness of people enjoying a walk are in harmony, has a space to enjoy reading mingling with the nature. Yangcheon Park Book Shelter with a shape of a windmill that the three curved lines towards insidestand back to back and surround by putting the cylinder bookshelf as a pivot, is a space wherethe beauty of curves is emphasized. Along the curved lines, which seems like they’re embracingthe park, they’ve made large windows, so it’s possible to bodily enjoy the nature of the park insidethe library.
