en.name: NaeSup Library
en.summary: A Bridge that Links Town and Park, NaeSup Library
en.description: ‘NaeSup Library’, which has opened to commemorate the 100 th anniversary of a poet, Yun Dong-ju’s birth brought the name from the front phrase of his poem, ‘A new path’. The library, locatedbetween the residential area where the multi-household houses are crowded and an azure park, isconnecting the town and the park as the verse of the poem, ‘beyond the hill, into the village’. The library appearance of inverted trapezoid has a green exterior as the forest beyond the library. Stair-type bookshelf, created along the steep slope of an apperance is the characteristic of 'NaeSup Library'.
en.hours:
Tuesday to Friday 09:00~22:00
Saturday to Sunday 09:00~18:00

en.name: Gyeongui Line Book Street
en.summary: A book-themed street where you can enjoy a quiet stroll away from the city center. It is also a place where you can participate in various programs such as themed walk & talks related to books every month.
en.description: Gyeongui Line Book Street is a well-known cultural hub with a book theme at Hongdae Station along the Gyeongui Line. It is also a place where you can participate in various programs such as themed walk & talks related to books every month. You can even meet different authors and talk to them. Many people enjoy the warm sunshine and take a leisurely stroll through Gyeongui Line Book Street.

en.name: Malli-dong
en.summary: The Malli-dong neighborhood, located near Seoul Station, has been gaining popularity ever since the opening of Seoullo 7071, a sky garden and pedestrian road.
en.description: The Malli-dong neighborhood, located near Seoul Station, has been gaining popularity ever since the opening of Seoullo 7071, a sky garden and pedestrian road. This historic district of Seoul is home to a variety of restaurants with delectable food and trendy coffee shops. This area dates back to the state of Joseon, so the locals associate it with the history of the city.
en.address: The Manri-ro area in Jung-gu, Seoul

en.name: Eunpyeong Hanok Village
en.summary: A picturesque hanok village located at the foot of Bukhansan Mountain in Jingwan-dong
en.description: Located in Jingwan-dong of Eunpyeong-gu, the Eunpyeong Hanok Village captures a quaint, serene landscape with the Bukhansan Mountain serving as the backdrop for the modern, neatly-built hanoks. The village is set in greater Seoul in the vicinity of Yeonsinnae and Ilsan. If you take a snapshot from the middle of the road between the tall hanok structures, it'll give you the feeling of standing on the set of some historical film set during the Joseon Dynasty. There are also plenty of sites to see if you walk up from the hanok village along the deck path that will lead you to the Jingwansa Temple, Literature Museum, and more!

en.name: Seocho Tourist Information Center
en.summary: No need to go far! Experience various programs and make cherishable memories right by Gangnam Station.
en.description: Making Memories at Seocho Tourist Information Center Venue: Between Exits 9 and 10 of Gangnam Station Target Audience: Open to everyone (Korean nationals & foreigners) Programming: VR tour, chromakey photo zone, hanbok and Korean instruments hands-on programs, letter-sending, etc. Fee: Free admissions

en.name: Daerim Market & Gamjaguk Street
en.summary: With restaurants inside Daerim Market selling gamjaguk made by boiling pork ribs, potatoes, and cabbage since mid-1980s, the area became popularized as Gamjaguk Street.
en.description: Gamjaguk is a must-eat dish for those visiting Eungam-dong! With restaurants inside Daerim Market selling gamjaguk made by boiling pork ribs, potatoes, and cabbage since mid-1980s, the area became popularized as Gamjaguk Street. With competition getting fierce, restaurants started to experiment and develop their own unique broth recipes, eventually leading to more and more people knowing about Eungam-dong's gamjaguk.

en.name: Seorae Village
en.summary: Seorae Village is named for the "seoriseori," or winding and twisting streams that once flowed next to the village.
en.description: Seorae Village is named for the " seoriseori," or winding and twisting streams that once flowed next to the village. Today, the area is better known for the multitude of French restaurants, cafes, wine bars, and trendy stores that thrive here. There is also a thriving community of French expats here, and of the 1,000 or so French nationals in Korea, half of them reside in Seorae Village. The village is located close to the Gangnam neighborhood.

en.name: Insadong
en.summary: Nowhere exudes more local and traditional charm than Insa-dong, a quaint neighborhood in the center of Seoul
en.description: Nowhere exudes more local and traditional charm than Insa-dong, a quaint neighborhood in the center of Seoul that transports visitors back to a time when women wore hanbok and men rode horses. With its wooden tea houses, boutique galleries and street vendors selling traditional snacks, a stroll through Insa-dong is mandatory for all visitors, especially on Sundays when the streets become traffic free and come alive with street performances, buskers and throngs of young and old who have come to experience one of Seoul’s most fascinating and creative neighborhoods. While the entertainment here is free, Insa-dong is also one of the best places in Seoul to purchase traditional Korean art, products, and other souvenirs, as it is filled with antique shops, art galleries, traditional stationery shops, handicraft shops, pottery and porcelain shops, bookstores, and art supply stores. Insa-dong is also home to many traditional restaurants and tea houses. Frequently Asked Questions about Insadong-gil Are there any tourist attractions worth visiting near Insadong-gil? These are the following tourist attractions around Insadong-gil. • Ssamzie-gil • Nagwon Instrument Arcade • Cheonggyecheon Stream What is the nearest subway station to Insadong-gil? The nearest subway stations to Insadong-gil are Anguk Station (Subway Line 3 - Exit 6), Jongno 3-ga Station (Subway Line 1,3, and 5 - Exit 5), and Jonggak Station (Subway Line 1 - Exit 11)

en.name: Hongdae
en.summary: Lit up by neon signs that buzz late into the night, evenings in Seoul have a creative energy that sucks people in crowds.
en.description: Hongdae is the scene where Korean culture, both pop and indie, manifests, especially at night. More information on planning a Sangam day trip can be soon found at K-stars and their K-style if the Korean Wave has washed over you, then there’s no better place to tread the path of such tastemakers as Hongdae, the live-wire district of music and art culture. Whether you’ve come on your own or with equally eager friends, the ever-trending university area remains the only place in Seoul where you can transitionfrom daytime exploring to nighttime adventures just as easily as you shuffle through your K-Pop playlist. Shopping in Hongdae Across the street and around the corner is a three-story store aptly named Around the Corner, Its multi-designer displays only cover two floors, but the smaller selection gives customers room to consider the subtler hip-hop motifs and mixed prints that punctuate the street wear-filled racks. Remember, just because Hongdae is more casual and “free” than, say, Gangnam or Apgujeong, doesn’t mean fashion doesn’t matter. The vibe you can see from the stores and the people on the streets, is effortless withan edge of the true Hongdae touch. You can see more of that in the quintessential Hongdae institution Aland, and the up-and-coming company Underst ar.

en.name: Itaewon
en.summary: Located smack-dab in the center of Seoul, Itaewon is home for the majority of expats that reside in Korea, making Itaewon a mini melting pot of cultures and religions from all over the world.
en.description: Korea is one of the most ethnically homogeneous countries in the world, but you'd never know that walking down the streets of Itaewon. Located smack-dab in the center of Seoul, Itaewon is home for the majority of expats that reside in Korea, making Itaewon a mini melting pot of cultures and religions from all over the world. The Seoul Central Mosque is also located in Itaewon along with a number of halal food stores, and large numbers of US military personnel can be seen here as the Yongsan Garrison that is stationed nearby. Due to the area’s diverse inhabitants, Itaewon has become one of the most cosmopolitan areas in Seoul boasting restaurants, shopping and nightlife that are equally diverse and cater to international tastes, attracting many other foreigners and tourists. It is safe to say that Itaewon is almost better known by foreigners and non-Korean residents than Koreans. Itaewon is known as the place to go when you want to get your foreign food fix. Restaurants featuring cuisine from all over the world can be found here including Indian, Thai, Pakistani, Greek, German, French, Italian, Australian, English, American, and Mexican, cuisines which are not easily found in Korea. Itaewon is also famous for its nightlife. Among foreigners, it is often considered the most popular area of Seoul for bars and clubs other than Hongdae. A range of drinking establishments can be found here including pubs, wine bars, hip-hop clubs, salsa clubs, lounges and cafes. Most stores in Korea offer clothing that fit Asian builds well but are unfortunately too small to fit those with “Western builds”. This leaves many of those with bigger and taller builds struggling to find clothing that fit. Fortunately many of the stores in Itaewon offer imported clothing in sizes that are difficult to find elsewhere in Korea. And if you still can’t find what you want, experienced tailors can create customized clothing. Itaewon also specializes in leather and fur goods, luggage and handbags, as well as jewelry and antique furniture. Trinkets and souvenirs can also be found here. Itaewon boasts some 100 antique stores clustered together on a single street. Originally these stores only dealt with second-hand U.S. Army furniture, but nowadays the selections at the stores have expanded to include antique furniture from around the world. Frequently Asked Questions about Itaewon What are the recommended attractions in Itaewon? These are the following tourist attractions around Itaewon. • Haengbangchon Alley • Leeum Art Museum • Itaewon Antique Furniture Street More Itaewon-related tourism content below • Filming locations of the drama Itaewon Class • Go to Itaewon, the most exotic street in Seoul How can I get to Itaewon Street using public transportation? You can get to Itaewon by subway and bus • Subway: Noksapyeong Station (Subway Line 6), Itaewon Station (Subway Line 6) • Bus: 143, 401, 405, 406, 100, 100A Korea University, 100B Kookmin University, 400, 402, 421, 740, N72, N75, Yongsan 01, Yongsan 02, Yongsan 03 (As of 2025) What festivals are held on Itaewon Street? Every October, the 'Itaewon Global Village Festival' is held on the streets of Itaewon. The Itaewon Global Village Festival is Seoul's main global street culture festival where people from all over the world gather and can enjoy unique and various cultures.

en.name: Daehak-ro
en.summary: Daehak-ro (sometimes spelled Daehangno) is Seoul's theater and performing arts district.
en.description: Daehak-ro (sometimes spelled Daehangno) is Seoul's theater and performing arts district. Daehak-ro is the name of the neighborhood and the area's main road. Daehak-ro Street stretches from Jongno 4ga to Hyehwa Rotary. There are numerous theaters and performance venues of all sizes located throughout the area. Visitors who are fans of theater, musicals, and music should head to Daehak-ro to get their fill of cultural experiences.

en.name: Seoul Music
en.summary: Opened in 1972, Seoul Music continues to exist in the underground shopping center below City Hall.
en.description: Opened in 1972, Seoul Music continues to exist in the underground shopping center below City Hall. A witness to the explosive growth of Korea's music market, this store has remained standing, taking in and remembering all the ups and down of history.

en.name: Nature Poem
en.summary: Nature Poem is a six-story commercial gallery located in the heart of Gangnam's posh Cheongdam-dong neighborhood.
en.description: Nature Poem is a six-story commercial gallery located in the heart of Gangnam's posh Cheongdam-dong neighborhood. Cheongdam-dong is famous for its abundance of premium designer stores. Nature Poem is located near many art galleries and high-end luxury stores, making a visit to Nature Poem a convenient starting point for a tour of Gangnam. Gallery GO, the Nam June Paik Museum and Gallery Jang are all nearby.

en.name: Seo Gallery
en.summary: The Seo Gallery is an arts gallery in Banpo-dong, Seoul.
en.description: The Seo Gallery is an arts gallery in Banpo-dong, Seoul. Its exhibitions cover a wide variety of different mediums including, but not limited to, painting, sculpture, photography, architecture, design, and fashion. The gallery also provides various programs to support both older artists and to foster new artists.

en.name: Mullae Art Village
en.summary: The Mullae Art Village is an area that was once known for its steel foundries but has transformed into an artists' village in recent years.
en.description: The Mullae Art Village is an area that was once known for its steel foundries but has transformed into an artists' village in recent years. There are numerous artists' studios and workshops here as well as great cafes and restaurants. Nearly every corner of the area is adorned with colorful murals and outdoor sculptures. There is much to see and photograph here. On weekends, most studios and workshops close so visitors will get a rare chance to see artwork that adorns window shutters and doors.

en.name: TETEROTSALON
en.summary: A must-visit place for a Seoul trip. Landmark for K-fashion, Korean gifts.
en.description: TETEROTSALON, one of the well-known K-fashion brands, is located on Hanok Street in Ikseon-dong, a hot place in Seoul It has a high quality as a brand where designers based on the traditional Korean design style gather to produce their own clothes. It sells various unique gift products from Korea and clothing, so it is a good place to shop for gifts and souvenirs. If you are looking for unique Korean gifts during a tour, please visit.
en.fee: 5,000 won to 200,000 won. Wide price range.

en.name: Gaemi Supermarket
en.summary: A supermarket loved more by foreigners with a 120-year history
en.description: Opened in the 1900s, Gaemi Super has a history with the surrounding sewing industry. There were many sewing shops leading from Seoul Station to Namdaemun Market. The employees of the sewing shops were the customers of the store, but in the 2000s, the sewing industry became specialized and the store's sales plummeted. However, in 2015, foreigners started coming to the area, and they started taking pictures with them, and it became a culture. As a testament to this, one wall of Gaemi Super is covered with photos of foreign customers and the owner.

en.name: Chunchusa
en.summary: A graduation gown store to help you remember the special times
en.description: Chunchusa is a 60-year-old gown shop that has been in business for three generations. Numerous degree gowns in a variety of materials and colors fill one side of the store, and a separate room is dedicated to ironing the gowns. Chunchusa has been specializing in degree gowns since 1960. In a year, the company rents out about 60,000 gowns. Chunchusa enjoys making clothes that commemorate someone's special moment, and this joy is reflected in work.

en.name: Yeonhee Photo Studio
en.summary: A photo studio in Yeonhui-dong, ideal for quick shots and photo editing on the spot
en.description: Founded in the 1950s, Yeonhee Photo Studio has been in operation for over 65 years with three generations of owners. Offering high-quality photos and quick retouching services, Yeonhee Photo Studio is popular with both Korean and foreign customers. There is a powder room where you can apply makeup and do your hair before your photo shoot, and they have a wide selection of headbands and hair accessories. Yeonhee Photo Studio is considered to be a popular spot for "employment photos," and it is said that having your job application photo taken here increases your chances of getting hired.

en.name: Haechang Tailor Shop
en.summary: Haechang Tailor shop is Sogong-dong’s oldest tailor shop with over 90 years of history.
en.description: Haechang Tailor shop is Sogong-dong’s oldest tailor shop with over 90 years of history. Having started its origin in Bosu-dong, Busan back in 1929, it moved locations to Sogong-dong, Seoul in 1945 and developed an impressive list of clientele including many historical figures in Korea. Haechang Tailor Shop was a beloved shop of many prominent political figures in Korean history. This shop was able continue to maintain business due to their high quality service and suits. Through constant communication with their customers, the shop make suits that accurately reflect the individual customer's style through details. One of Korea's first tailor shop, many students who used to learn and work in this store has set up their own tailor shops throughout Korea.

en.name: Yuil Oriental Medicine Clinic
en.summary: A traditional oriental medicine clinic offering acupuncture and herbal medicine prescriptions
en.description: Yuil Oriental Medicine Clinic was founded in 1945 by Dr. Lee Taek-sung, the father of the current president, and has remained in the same location ever since. The Jongno-gu area was originally densely populated with oriental medicine clinics and herbal medicine shops, and at one point there were 300 of them. Today, the number of clinics has decreased, but the only cli nic still stands. It is the 'only' oriental medicine clinic, as the name suggests, that has been practicing the old acupuncture methods that are different from other clinics. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

en.name: Dol Record
en.summary: A secondhand record store where precious memories are hidden
en.description: Since 1975, Dole Records has been selling LP, CD, and cassette tapes that contain someone's memories. Word of mouth has spread like wildfire about this treasure trove, and it continues to attract record lovers to this day. It is one of the few remaining record stores in Seoul that not only retains its original appearance, but also has a large selection of LPs, cassette tapes, and CDs that symbolize Korean popular music from the 70s to the 90s.

en.name: Daegu Sesame Oil
en.summary: Sesame oil's delicious aroma spreading through Bukchon Hanok Village
en.description: When walking along Gyedong-gil in Bukchon, there is a place that stops you in your tracks with its savory sesame oil smell. The owner, who has more than 40 years of oil experience, squeezes and sells the oil himself, and has been running a sesame oil shop in the same place since 1975. There are many regular customers, but foreign tourists often come here to buy sesame oil after seeing it in magazines or on TV. They sell sesame and perilla oils that are no more than a week old, so you can be sure of their freshness. They also deliver nationwide.

en.name: Munhwa Barber Shop
en.summary: Munhwa Barber Shop has been around for 78 years.
en.description: Munhwa Barber Shop has been around for 78 years. Both the exterior and interior appearance of this shop has remained unchanged over the years, leading to an atmospheric shop which leads visitors to reminisce about the past.

en.name: Tongmungwan
en.summary: The Korea’s oldest bookstore with national treasure-level cultural artifacts
en.description: Tongmungwan is an old bookstore that opened in 1934, and has been opening for three generations. It is a bookstore that discovers, evaluates, analyzes, distributes, and publishes ancient Korean books, and has discovered numerous cultural assets such as "Wolin Seokbo" and "Independent Newspaper." It is currently run by Lee Jong-un, the grandson of founder and first director Lee Geom-ro. The main customers are those who study and study ancient books, collectors who invest in the value of ancient books, and Japanese and Chinese tourists who are familiar with Chinese characters, according to the commission. • This place has been selected as a ' Seoul Future Heritage '. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.

en.name: Napcheong Bronzeware
en.summary: A store that sells bangjja products made by a national intangible cultural heritage master
en.description: Napcheongnotjeon is a brassware shop that continues the organic production method of the Napcheong region of North Pyongan Province. It has been selling Bangja organic brassware in Insadong since 1986 and has been practicing the method for more than half a century, making it a favorite among locals and foreigners alike. Most of the products are made by Lee Bong-joo, who was the first person in Korea to be designated as an Important Intangible Cultural Property No. 77 in 1983, and his eldest son, Lee Hyung-geun, who took over the business in 2015.

en.name: Gukseon Otchil
en.summary: Since 1977, this place has been selling lacquerware inlaid with mother-of-pearl.
en.description: This store has been selling lacquerware since 1977. The store has a history of 40 years and is run by two generations. The first-generation owner came to Seoul alone when he was 19 years old and learned the craft for the first time at a lacquer workshop that solves room and board. Located in Gwangjang Market, the project was acquired by his son, a cultural asset function, under the new name of national lacquer. Today, the business exports mother-of-pearl products to countries around the world and has developed its reputation as a traditional craft shop representing Korean style. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.(https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

en.name: Pungwoldang
en.summary: Pungwoldang is a classical music store and cultural space in Cheongdam-dong.
en.description: Pungwoldang is a classical music store and cultural space in Cheongdam-dong. Visitors can shop for classical music CDs and books on classical music. There is even a listening room dubbed "Pungwolchae." Pungwoldang hosts cultural events such as lectures on classical music, video screenings, and musical events. Pungwoldang also has a cafe that sells light refreshments.

en.name: Hongdae Free Market
en.summary: Hongdae (Hongik University) Free Market is a marketplace for young artists. The market is run in a flea market format, but while a typical flea market sells second-hand goods, this free market sells only genuinely creative artwork.
en.description: Hongdae (Hongik University) Free Market is a marketplace for young artists. The market is run in a flea market format, but while a typical flea market sells second-hand goods, the Free Market sells only genuinely creative artwork. Since 2002, the market has been held every Saturday and has since become the prime cultural hotspot on Hongdae street, and a venue for performances by indie bands and different cultural events. The Free Market also introduces organizations who work for public good, hosts tours and workshops, and hosts the Afternoon Stage for local artists and musicians to perform at.
en.hours: Open Saturdays from March to November, 13:00 - 18:00 KST

en.name: Kwanchenru Street: The Little Chinese Quarter of Seoul
en.summary: Unknown to most, this little Chinese quarter in the heart of Seoul is home to some amazing authentic and traditional Chinese restaurants.
en.description: Kwanchenru Street is an unofficial cultural district located in Myeong-dong that is home to incredible Chinese restaurants and stores. Kwanchenru is the Chinese pronunciation of the Korean word "gwancheonga", which means the street in front of a government office. At one of end of Kwanchenru is the Chinese Embassy. Authentic, delicious Chinese food can be had here and there are several famous restaurants here such as Din Tai Fung. There are also several shops selling Chinese antiques, souvenirs, and books. Kwanchenru Street is a well-kept secret for some of the best Chinese restaurants in Seoul.

en.name: Songridan-gil
en.summary: Walking course from Seokchon Lake Dongho to Songpanaru Station
en.description: Let's relax at the atmospheric terrace cafe with the beautiful Seokchon Lake. Lotte World, Lotte Tower, and nearby apartments offer stunning views at night.

en.name: Gyeongnidan-gil
en.summary: Between Itaewon and Haebangchon, the road from the Armed Forces Financial Management Corps to the Grand Hyatt Seoul and its surrounding alleys
en.description: Although it is part of Itaewon-dong, it is a famous street because of its different atmosphere from Itaewon! It is a cultural and youthful space famous for its diverse and unique food, and there are more bars and cafes with good atmospheres than regular restaurants, so it is a place that many foreigners staying in Korea visit.

en.name: Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Center
en.summary: Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall, built as a residential and commercial building in the 1960s, appeared as "Geumga Plaza" in the drama Vincenzo and has become a hot place to visit ever since.
en.description: Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall, built as a residential and commercial building in the 1960s, appeared as "Geumga Plaza" in the drama Vincenzo and has become a hot place to visit ever since. This shopping mall is considered to be the first electronics shopping center in Korea. Its name "Sewoon" means "a place that collects the energy of the world." Nowadays, visitors can find the popular cafes of the Euljiro district here, such as Horangi Cafe. Additionally, from the rooftop of the Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall, visitors can see the fantastic night views of Namsan Tower, Cheonggyecheon Stream, and the Jongno district. Visit Sewoon Cheonggye Shopping Mall and the popular cafes in the Euljiro district as you recall scenes from your favorite TV series.

en.name: Cheongdamdong Fashion Street
en.summary: Cheongdam currently boasts the world's major luxury brands lined up neatly for your shopping pleasure.
en.description: Cheongdam currently boasts the world's major luxury brands lined up neatly for your shopping pleasure. Present are renowned brands such as Louis Vuitton, Prada, Cartier, and Burberry, but also avant-garde international and Korean designers such as Martin Margiela and Son Jung Wan. The boutiques installed here are all about providing clients with lifestyle experiences that would have you come back and spend lots more of your money -- Seoul’s luxury experience is all about excellent service and hospitality. Many of the shops also operate their own restaurants and cafes inside, and regularly launch exclusive promotions and events in an effort to close the distance between the brands and the consumers. Cheongdam is also known for its cluster of beauty and hair salons with floors and floors of beauty experts offering complete "Seoulite" makeovers, nails, face or body massages, hairdos.This is where Korean celebrities come to get their makeup done (as well as re-model their body parts - have we mentioned that Seoul is also the mecca of plastic surgery?), which is why Cheongdam is also called "Celebrity Street".

en.name: Geumcheon Course
en.summary: The Geumcheon-gu area is a great place to find IT products, cultural items, activities, good food, and more due to the cluster of big shopping malls, such as Mario Outlet, W Mall, and Hyundai outlet.
en.description: The Geumcheon-gu area is a great place to find IT products, cultural items, activities, good food, and more due to the cluster of big shopping malls. Mario Outlet carries famous brands and good quality items, but always seeks to offer the biggest discount possible 365 days a year. W Mall is a leading fashion outlet that carries women's clothing, men's clothing, casual wear, fashion accessories, sportswear, outdoor wear, and children's clothing. 300 well-known Korean brands are gathered at this one place and offered to customers at a reasonable price. At the Hyundai outlet in Gasan, you have access to famous brands for up to 80% off all year long. As part of a way to establish more creative spaces in the Seoul, the Seoul Art Space was created by remodeling a printing plant in October 2009. This space is intended to encourage and help artists step into their gifts, while also allowing the public to enjoy art and culture through a variety of programs.

en.name: Garosu-gil Road
en.summary: Garosu-gil has quickly became one of Seoul's hottest neighborhoods in recent years.
en.description: Garosu-gil has quickly became one of Seoul's hottest neighborhoods in recent years. 20 years ago, this place was once a densely populated area filled with galleries and packed with designer shops. At one point, many film companies spotted the area, and at other times, various artists set up shop here. So there plenty of neat, older shops in the Garosu-gil area. Additionally, there are many fashion stores that have become quite popular. The stores in the area are diverse, from antique furniture stores to bookstores selling foreign books. It is also a good walking area. It's also very easy for visitors to come across their new favorite cafes while strolling around the neighborhood. In addition to clothing stores, visitors can find plenty of exhibitions and galleries to check out. Frequently Asked Questions about Garosu-gil What is the nearest subway station to Garosu-gil? The closest subway stations to Garosu-gil are Sinsa Station (Sinbundang Line, Subway Line 3 - Exit 8) and Apgujeong Station (Subway Line 3 - Exit 4). Where is the closest Hangang Park to Garosu-gil? The nearest Hangang Park to Garosu-gil is Jamwon Hangang Park .

en.name: Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street
en.summary: The street is packed with home and foreign brand-name stores targeting all ages from teenagers to the older generations and offering good quality products at very moderate prices.
en.description: Located at subway line 8 Munjeong station, Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street is considered to be Korea's first outlet shopping district. The street began when shops selling off excess clothing stock opened here one by one. After walking about 500 meters from exit 1 of Munjeong Station, a cowboy statue first welcomes visitors. From here, the 2.5 kilometers of Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street begin, also known as the first fashion avenue. Both sides of the street are full with over 200 brand-name shops, making it easy to browse several famous brands at once. Always popular with shoppers are the 100 individual shops, as well as the multi-fashion malls such as Modes, Dump etc. or the outlet shops such as Cheil Industries Inc. and LG Fashion. When you start to feel tired from shopping, Zelkova Park, situated just behind Munjeong-dong Office is the perfect place to take a rest. The park has a 600-year-old zelkova tree and provides refreshing rest areas. There are many restaurants, cafes, amusement arcades, food courts etc. located nearby, providing lots of interesting things to see, do and eat. As the nation's oldest outlet street, various festivals and cultural events are frequently held on Munjeong-dong Rodeo Street.

en.name: Mokdong Rodeo Street
en.summary: Mokdong Rodeo Street features fashion outlets which offer a wide range of well-known brands at discounted prices throughout the year.
en.description: Mokdong Rodeo Street features fashion outlets which offer a wide range of well-known brands at discounted prices throughout the year. The street is easily accessible as it is situated close to Mokdong Station, Subway Line 5. Since it was formed in 1994, the reputation of Mokdong Rodeo Street has as a fashion and cultural district has steadily grown. It is also a popular shopping destination for overseas tourists as they can purchase high-quality brands at discounted prices. Situated in the middle of Mokdong apartment complex, Mokdong Rodeo Street is the originator of outlet stores, but has many features that are different from other outlets. First of all, clothing stores are grouped together by category into themed streets, for example, ladies’, men’s, casual and golf wear, rather than being scattered individually. Furthermore, as most stores are located on ground level, it is the perfect place for window-shopping as you take a stroll. Everything about Rodeo Street has been designed with the shoppers’ convenience in mind.

en.name: Yongsan Mill
en.summary: Running its business near Ichon-dong's railroad for the past 30 years, Yongsan Mill was created by an owner who used to work in a rice cake factory.
en.description: Running its business near Ichon-dong's railroad for the past 30 years, Yongsan Mill was created by an owner who used to work in a rice cake factory. Able to make any kind of rice cake using high quality ingredients, Yongsan Mill has become a beloved place for many of its local residents. Not only do they make rice cake, but they also makes sesame oil and crushes red pepper flakes like any other regular mill.

en.name: Brothers' Blacksmith Workshop
en.category: History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
en.summary: A store run by a human cultural asset where intellectuals, artists, and professors visit
en.description: This 40-year-old blacksmith shop is a 5-minute walk from Search Station. It is run by brothers and produces everything from farming tools to building tools. In addition to making goods, they also do various things related to Korean culture. If you want to experience old Korean farming tools and traditional tools, we recommend you stop by. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)
en.hours: 07:30~18:30 (closes earlier in winter and later in summer)

en.name: Sewoon Shopping Center
en.category: History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
en.summary: The Sewoon Shopping Center was founded in 1968 as Korea's first electronics market under the mission of creating a thriving business community complex and has been around for over 40 years.
en.description: The Sewoon Shopping Center was founded in 1968 as Korea's first electronics market under the mission of creating a thriving business community complex and has been around for over 40 years. The center reached its height during the 1970s & 80s as Korea's "go-to" electronics market but has also experienced a few low points along the way. However, in 2017, the Dasi Sewoon Project advocated for the second rise of the market as a "Maker City" that embraces both the creative manufacturing and creative printing industries. The market offers not only a wide selection of electronics and electrical products such as appliances, parts, audio devices, security cameras, arcade games, karaoke equipment and lighting equipment, but it is also home to a variety of other sites and attractions, such as the Sewoon Rooftop where Seoul's past and present converge into a single panoramic view, the sky-deck walkway, which is open to the public and crosses the Cheonggyecheon Stream, Sewoon Hall, a culture complex celebrating Joseon Dynasty cultural values, and the Cheonggye Sanghoe, a market filled with items specific to different regions and communities throughout the country.

en.name: Boutique Monaco
en.summary: Boutique Monaco is an avant-gard penthouse and apartment building that has been used as a filming location for Korean TV shows.
en.description: Boutique Monaco is an avant-gard penthouse and apartment building that has been used as a filming location for Korean TV shows. Fans of "My Love from the Star" will recognize this building as the location where Do Minjun (Kim Soo Hyun) throws Lee Jae-gyung (Sin Seong Rok) out the window. There is a cafe on the ground floor and an outdoor garden between every floor. The building has become a local landmark due to its unique architectural design.

en.name: BoomBim Hanbok Experience
en.summary: BoomBim Hanbok Experience is a hanbok rental shop with a huge range of different hanbok available for patrons.
en.description: BoomBim Hanbok Experience is a hanbok rental shop with a huge range of different hanbok available for patrons. BoomBim is conveniently located next to the major Seoul tourist attractions such as Lotte World, Lotte Tower, Seokchon Lake, and Olympic Park. With indoor attractions and outdoor attractions nearby, no matter what the weather, visitors will be able to comfortably tour Seoul's attractions while dressed up in hanbok. Rent a hanbok and make memories in Seoul!

en.name: Yeong Bin Gwan (The Shilla Seoul)
en.summary: Owned and operated by The Shilla Seoul, Yeong Bin Gwan is a unique dining and event space located in the hotel grounds.
en.description: Owned and operated by The Shilla Seoul, Yeong Bin Gwan is a unique dining and event space located in the hotel grounds. Built in the style of a hanok (traditional Korean house), the two-story facility was originally designed to accommodate foreign VIPS, and can now be used for a variety of dining functions, including banquets, parties, and corporate dinners.

en.name: Itaewon Global Village Festival
en.summary: From October 17-18, the "2015 Itaewon Global Village Festival" will  take place in Itaewon, an area that is considered to be a special tourist zone.
en.description: From October 17-18, the "2015 Itaewon Global Village Festival" will take place in Itaewon, an area that is considered to be a special tourist zone. The festival will be one dynamic event. The highlight is definitely the global village parade, then there is the fashion show with traditional clothing, a "DJ festival" that has the unconditional support of the younger generation, a chance to see the culture of different countries, and also a chance to try foods from different nations as well. For the first time this year, the audience will be able to participate in quizzes, a traditional form of tug-of-war, a Korean game of popping a plastic balloon-like structure, and other events that are tailored for a large sum of people so that everyone can join in at once. The main stage will be at Noksapyeong station, but there will be separate smaller stages all around the Itaewon area and Bogwang-ro, where you can see traditional folk performances, participate in the global village quiz, see street performances, and various other forms of entertainment.

en.name: Seoul Bamdokkaebi Night Market 2015
en.summary: From October 1-17, Yeouido Hangang Park will be hosting a late night market where you can eat from food trucks, browse through creative items for sale, and enjoy fun performances. The exact dates are as follows: October 1-2, 8-20, and 16-17. The market will be open from 6 pm until 12 am.
en.description: Late night market at the Hangang (River)! From October 1-17, Yeouido Hangang Park will be hosting a late night market where you can eat from food trucks, browse through creative items for sale, and enjoy fun performances. The exact dates are as follows: October 1-2, 8-20, and 16-17. The market will be open from 6 pm until 12 am.

en.name: Run@SeoulWeek
en.summary: Seoul Metropolitan Government invites global citizens to participate in interactive campaign to give missions to the runners so they can accomplish various missions given and deliver lively images of Seoul.
en.description: Seoul Metropolitan Government invites global citizens to participate in interactive campaign to give missions to the runners so they can accomplish various missions given and deliver lively images of Seoul.

en.name: Seoul Independent Film Festival 2014
en.summary: Known as the most representative collection of independent films in Korea, the Seoul Independent Film Festival boasts a history dating back to 1975. It provides a platform for up and coming independent film directors to present their work and a means for audiences in Seoul to quench their cultural and artitstic thirst.
en.description: Known as the most representative collection of independent films in Korea, the Seoul Independent Film Festival boasts a history dating back to 1975. It provides a platform for up and coming independent film directors to present their work and a means for audiences in Seoul to quench their cultural and artitstic thirst.

en.name: Seoul Metro Stamp Tour
en.summary: Visit tourist attractions in Seoul and take photos in order to receive a stamp on your booklet. The first 1,000 people to complete all the courses will be given souvenirs.
en.description: Seoul Metro Stamp Tour/ Tour Seoul via subway Visit tourist attractions in Seoul and take photos in order to receive a stamp on your booklet. The first 1,000 people to complete all the courses will be given souvenirs. Stamp Station Locations Tourist Attractions Seoul Station (Lines 1, 4) Culture Station Seoul 284 (former Seoul Station), Namdaemun Gate (Sungnyemun Gate), Namdaemun Market Hoehyeon Station or Myeongdong Station (Line 4) Mt. Namsan, Namsan Seoul Tower, Myeong-dong Shopping District, Myeongdong Cathedral KTO Tourist Information Center Cheonggyecheon Stream, Gwanghwamun Square, Korea Tourism Organization,TIC Course 2: The Street of Youth Stamp Station Locations Tourist Attractions Hongik University Station (Line 2) Hongdae area including Hongdae Street, Hongdae Flea Market, etc. Sinchon Station or Ewha Womans University Station (Line 2) Street between Sinchon and Ewha Womans University (Car-free Street/Myeongmul-geori Street) Course 3: A Glimpse of History Stamp Station Locations Tourist Attractions Gyeongbokgung Palace Station (Line 3) Sajikdan, Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae, Gyeongbokgung Palace, National Museum of Korean Contemporary History, Hangeul Gaon-gil, Seoul Museum of History, Samcheongdong-gil Road City Hall Station (Lines 1, 2) Jeongdong-gil Road, Deoksugung Doldam-gil (Deoksugung Stone-Wall Road), Deoksugung Palace Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony, Seoul Museum of Art KTO Tourist Information Center Bosingak, Jogyesa Temple, Tapgol Park, Insa-dong (Ssamziegil) Course 4: Going Beyond Tradition and Toward the Future Stamp Station Locations Tourist Attractions Hyehwa Station (Line 4) Ihwa-dong Mural Village, Naksan Park, Dongdaemun Seonggwak (Fortress Wall) - Naksan Course, Daehangno (University Street) Dongdaemun Station (Lines 1, 4) Dongdaemun Gate (Heunginjimun Gate), Dongdaemun Market Dongdaemun History & Culture Park Station (Lines 2, 4) Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Dongdaemun History Museum, Klive (K-pop Hologram Concert Hall)

en.name: Seoul Fringe Festival
en.summary: Please be advised that dates are announced seasonally.
en.description: ※ The 2016 Schedule Is Coming Soon 2015 celebrates the 18th annual Seoul Fringe Festival, which began in 1998 as the "Independent Arts Festival." From August 1st through 9th, performances will take place at several different indoor and outdoor spaces in Hongdae and the World Cup Stadium. Hundreds of individuals and groups will perform theater, dance, pantomime, music and interdisciplinary performance art that combines multiple genres.
en.address: World Cup Stadium, 240, World Cup-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul

en.name: Gwanghwamun International Art Festival
en.summary: The Gwanghwamun International Art Festival (GIAF) is an annual art festival that aims to improve the quality of Korean art and pop culture.
en.description: The Gwanghwamun International Art Festival (GIAF) is an annual art festival that aims to improve the quality of Korean art and pop culture. The festival takes place from May 29 - June 24 at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts and The Story of King Sejong Exhibition Hall located in Gwanghwamun Square. The work of more than 500 domestic and international artists will be exhibited for people to enjoy. In addition to viewing the art exhibits, visitors will also be able to enjoy various performances and try different kinds of arts and crafts including ceramics, color therapy, silver handicrafts, leather handicrafts and more.

en.name: Music at the Royal Palace
en.summary: From May to October of each year, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ is held at Changdeokgung (Palace), Deoksugung (Palace), Gyeongbokgung (Palace) and Jongmyo (Royal Shrine).
en.description: Starting from May 4 until October 13, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ will be held at Changdeokgung (Palace), Deoksugung (Palace), Gyeongbokgung (Palace) and Jongmyo (Royal Shrine). After the first successful traditional arts performance in 2008, ｢Music in the Royal Palace｣ has become a permanant show since 2009. Every spring and autumn, each palace offers a wealth of cultural events to watch for both locals and foreigners who visit. ｢Music at the Royal Palace｣ not only provides entertainment for vistors with traditional musical performances and storytelling, but also offers visitors a chance to experience the elegance of palaces and the depth of traditional Korean arts by bringing culture, history and arts together. In order for viewers to truly experience the beauty and original atmosphere of the palace and music, the stage, sounds and lightings have all been reduced to a minimum. Experience the elegance of Court Music ｢Changdeokgung (Palace) Concert｣ Changdeokgung (Palace), designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, will be holding a very special concert. Vistors can take a stroll through Huwon, a garden of natural beauty, and enjoy the traditional music that fills the air. Vistors can watcch traditional court music every Sunday morning at Nakseonjae (the Queen's private residential area). For 270 years, the palace was home to the Joseon government and was also the favored residence of many Joseon Dynasty kings. This makes Changdeokgung (Palace) the longest-serving royal residential palace. Compared to other palaces, Changdeokgung is well-preserved and still has many of its original features. A particular virture of Changdeokgung is the way its buildings blend into the surrounding landscape. The World of Musical Storytelling ｢Deoksugung (Palace) Concert｣ Deoksugung (Palace), a place where the past and present coexist, will feature storytelling concerts for children. Every Saturday and Sunday, a fusion blend of folk music and folktales will be performed at Hamnyeongjeon (King Go Jong's sleeping quarters). Masterpieces like「The Little Prince」and 「The Giving Tree」are brilliantly recreated with traditional Korean music and animations, satisfying both the eyes and ears. The concert will bring back heartwarming memories for adults and create dreams and fantasies for children. What kind of music did kings listen to? ｢Gyeongbokgung (Palace) Concert｣ If a king still lived in Gyeongbokgung (Palace) today, what kind of music would he listen to? He would have likely enjoyed a wonderful musical culture that perserves tradition, yet embraces the music of today. Enjoy festivities of Court Music that best matches the ambience Gyeongbokgung. One of a kind music ｢Jongmyo Jeryeak with Commentary｣ Jongmyo jeryeak (Jongmyo Royal Ancestral Confucian Memorial Ceremony Music) is a ceremonial music that is dedicated to all kings of Joseon Dynasty. Jongmyo jeryeak was registered as the first Korea Cultural Heritage and is also registered with UNESCO World Intangible Cultural Heritage. It is difficult to listen the Jongmyo jeryeak aside from when it is annually performed at Jongmyo (Royal Shrine) once a year. ｢Jongmyojeryeak with a commentary｣ offers visitors the opportunity to not only listen to, but also to understand the history and culture of Jongmyo jeryeak through commentaries.

en.description: ※ The 2016 Schedule Is Coming Soon The Seoul International Fireworks Festival is held in early October of each year in front of the 63 City Building at Yeouido Hangang Park. This festival is one of Seoul's most popular fall events, and watching fireworks paint the sky and water in a breathtaking spectacle. The massive crowds that gather around the Hangang River also adds to the festive atmosphere. For the best views, head over to Yeouinaru Station and walk along the river until 63 City Building. If crowds make you uncomfortable, go to the following locations to enjoy the fireworks in relative peace and quiet: Ichon Hangang Park, Nodeul Island, Hangang Bridge Observatory, Sayukshin Park, Seonyudo Park, and Noryangjin Seafood Market Parking Tower. 2015 Schedule and Program 13:00~19:00: Public participation programs (Stage performances, etc.) 19:00~19:20: Opening Ceremony 19:20~19:35: U.S.A fireworks display 19:40~19:55: Phillipines fireworks display 20:00~20:40: Korea fireworks display 20:40~21:30: DJ performances (D zone) / Public participation "clean campaign"
